title: Roads That Shape Us
sentences: A city reveals its priorities not in its speeches but in the width and placement of its roads.
Where pavements narrow and lanes widen, pedestrians quietly learn that they matter somewhat less.
Infrastructure, once built, is stubborn, and it shapes behaviour long after its purpose fades.
A junction designed for speed will keep encouraging speed, regardless of any sign posted beside it.
People do not merely use a transport system; over time, they are quietly trained by it.
Public transport that runs rarely teaches its passengers, unfairly, to expect very little.
And yet the same city block can feel entirely different once a single bus route is added.
Arguably, the humblest crossing point does more for daily life than any grand new terminal.
To the extent that movement shapes mood, a badly planned street quietly narrows people's patience.
Rebuilding a road is slow and costly, but rebuilding the habits it created is slower still.
